Resolves #26

Tabs can opt into a close mark and Delete through `header.closable`. Both use `closeTab(index)`, with a synchronous `beforeTabClose` veto and a post-removal `tabClose` receipt. Docs now uses that policy instead of inspecting icon paths. Default tabs remain non-closable.

Related: #20390

Evidence: L3 (native Chromium interaction, focus and Docs consumer) → L3 required (generic closable-tab behavior). No Dock close-policy or cross-platform screen-reader certification claim.

## AC Evidence

No structured ACs on #26. This maps its implementation-intake ledger:

| Surface | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Opt-in headers and close intent | CI-covered: `unit/tab/Close.spec.mjs`; both header families, veto, event identity, invalid targets and listener mutation. |
| Pointer, keyboard and focus | CI-covered: `component/tab/Close.spec.mjs`; close without activation, default-off, veto, following-tab focus from headers or an in-panel Done button, empty-container continuation and external focus preservation. |
| Removal selection | CI-covered: `unit/tab/Removal.spec.mjs`; first/middle/last/only, ordinary and silent; native first/middle/last/only close controls. |
| Docs migration | CI-covered: actual Docs subclass in the close unit and component specs. |
| Pending lazy cards | CI-covered: deferred close/reorder/replacement-generation cases in the close spec, with existing `container/InsertLazyModule.spec.mjs` alias/retry controls. |
| Effect rendering | CI-covered: `unit/button/Effect.spec.mjs` excludes scheduler state from visual dependencies; native effect close reaches the DOM. |

## Deltas from ticket

The related removal repair selects index 0 when the first active card leaves and null when empty. Focus follows the next tab independently of the existing previous-neighbor selection policy. Pending Card imports follow their admitted occupant and cannot resurrect closed cards or overwrite replacements. Effect-button scheduling now runs after dependency collection, matching the functional-component boundary; this was required for native effect-header removal to settle.

Dock's render-only pane reparent uses silent removal and an explicit source render, so the new ordinary removal notification cannot issue a semantic selection against pending projection metadata. Superseded asynchronous tab activations also discard stale index/card notifications.

size-guard-growth: src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs — Preserve the existing render-only reparent boundary with silent removal and one explicit source render; no new Dock policy or authority.

## Test Evidence

Red/green controls: active-first/only removal failed before the repair; deferred imports reproduced neighbor overwrite, late resurrection and owner-destruction failure; native effect close removed the logical tab but retained its DOM until scheduling left the Effect tracking scope. The assertions were retained.

`agent-preflight`: not hosted in Engine; the shared PR baseline checks the body and source gates. Routine unit/component coverage belongs to CI.

Portal guide smoke at `c62abc882e`: H1, close guidance and the authored Mermaid diagram rendered (one non-error SVG). That receipt establishes the guide route and diagram; later focus prose is grounded in the native close controls.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge OR documented search (per guide §7.1):**

- **Challenge**: `closeTab` restores focus only when the header held it: `restoreFocus: header.containsFocus`.
  - Header and card are sibling subtrees, and `manager/Focus.mjs` (`setComponentFocus`) sets `containsFocus` only along the focus path.
  - That breaks the API's default-index use: a Close or Done control inside the active panel calls `tabs.closeTab()`. `restoreFocus` stays false, the focused element is destroyed with its card, and focus falls to the document body.
  - No arm in `component/tab/Close.spec.mjs` covers this; its focus arms are header focus, the only tab, the middle tab and an outside control. → RA-1.

I also actively looked for the following and found no concerns:
- **Subclasses whose own vdom lacks the close span:** `TabEnterButton` and `RevealOverlay` use the base vdom, and the span sits after the fixed `cn[4]` indicator lookup.
- **Callers that break on `loadModule`'s new null result:** `TearOut`, `form.Container#loadModules`, the Dock `Reconciler` and `container.Base` all ignore the value.
- **A worker round trip per keystroke from the new per-tab `keydown` listener:** there is none, because main already forwards every `keydown` (`src/main/DomEvents.mjs:14`, `:671`).
- **A duplicate close glyph in Docs:** its header icons are semantic.

- [x] PR description: framing matches what the diff substantiates (no overshoot)

- [x] `[RETROSPECTIVE]` tag: none in the PR
- [x] Linked anchors: the functional-component precedent the Deltas cite exists (`src/functional/component/Base.mjs:96`)

**Findings:** One drift outside those rows. The guide says "A programmatic close while focus is elsewhere leaves that focus alone"; that is false when focus sits inside the closing card. RA-1 repairs the code and the sentence together.
